title: Evaluate pause, rhythm and interaction motifs across meetings
summary: Extend the existing phrase-pause-continuation observations into alignment-aware rhythm and interaction research: response latency, overlap, backchannels and floor transitions. Timing and conversational roles remain descriptive evidence with explicit confounds.
out_of_scope: Assuming a timestamp gap is acoustic silence
Inferring untimed intervals or fixed individual rhythm from sparse turns
Combining correlated timing measures as independent identity votes
implementation: Reuse adjacent-word pause/motif and rate definitions, retaining timed/untimed coverage and the rule against skipping over an untimed word.

Define interaction episodes from procedural floor transitions and original-clock turn spans; distinguish response invitation, response onset, overlap, interruption and backchannel with source uncertainty.
Compute per-mode and per-context distributions with denominators and recording-group balance; separate chair/microphone delays from candidate person regularity.
Add alignment-quality and timing-perturbation controls, including partial word timing and chunk-boundary artifacts; no negative gap or overlap is silently converted to silence.
Evaluate each family and its interactions with procedure/lexical evidence on frozen cohorts and export only qualified descriptive support.

acceptance.criterion: Existing missing/partial timing semantics survive the extension.
acceptance.verification: Run untimed and partially timed lexical fixtures; no synthetic pauses or articulation rates are created.

acceptance.criterion: Response latency is conditioned on an evidenced interaction rather than arbitrary adjacent transcript rows.
acceptance.verification: Test chair invitation, unrelated new agenda item, overlapping speakers and missing turn boundaries.

acceptance.criterion: Timing noise and role/channel confounds are included in the reported effect.
acceptance.verification: Run alignment jitter and chair/shared-mic strata on the same queries and report changes and omissions.

acceptance.criterion: Multiple derived measures from one source occurrence do not become independent corroboration.
acceptance.verification: Inspect provenance-group weights and assessment evidence counts for several motifs from one turn.

tests: Untimed word between two timed words
Overlapping response with a negative apparent gap
Same speaker chairing versus giving prepared testimony
Many motifs from one long turn versus one short turn in another independent meeting
risks: ASR alignment artifacts may look stable across reused media.
Response timing may mostly reflect role/procedure or remote audio transport.

reuse.application: Reuse existing phrase–pause–continuation and original-clock limitations.

sources: User clarification, 2026-10-08, active Matter build: DIAT owns meeting learning; roughly 315 hours/5–10 recurring people is user-reported; crawler owns jurisdiction knowledge; private exported-data experiments only.
Original repository inputs: matterbrainstormspec; matterjevmesh; jevinmatter (brainstorming, not implementation evidence).
